name: AODBM
tagline: Deprecated 2011 dbm-style key-value library using immutable, append-only B+trees with versioned snapshots.
description: AODBM (Append Only Database Manager) is a small embeddable key-value library in the tradition of dbm, written in C with a Python binding by Daniel Waterworth in 2011. Every change appends new nodes of an immutable B+tree to the file, so each committed version stays readable as a snapshot and a commit fails cleanly if it was not based on the current version, giving ACID semantics with optimistic concurrency. The design is the same copy-on-write idea used by LMDB and CouchDB's storage, in a much simpler form. The author marked the repository deprecated and it has not changed since July 2011.
statusNote: Repository marked [DEPRECATED] by its author; no changes since July 2011. Use LMDB or another maintained embedded store.

scale.notes: Single file in a single process; the file only grows because old versions are never overwritten.

strengths: Immutable append-only B+tree keeps every committed version readable
Optimistic commits reject writes based on stale versions
Tiny C codebase that clearly illustrates copy-on-write storage
weaknesses: No compaction story, so files grow without bound
Single-process, single-file design with minimal tooling
